This game tries to squeeze money out of you at every turn. Save your time and money. Look elsewhere.

Returning player. I had heard the game had gotten better.

Turns out it really hasn't. The Oasis event has helped, sure, but it's still a crutch given to you that is actually aimed at the idea of you grinding day and night while you still have that gear and advantages.

BDO is really grindy, but unlike other alternatives, wich are also grindy, it only shows it's ugly head when you are deep in the activities.

BDO has awesome combat, pretty interesting lifeskill, and a great world to explore. You can do great things by starting little and turning them into something bigger... Except, that's the impression it gives to you. Soon you realize that in order turn that journey you started into something satisfactory you are gonna have to grind day and night for a looong time. 

The game literally forces you to leave it open and afk grinding in order to progress. And it just never ends. Each patch makes it worse.

You have a good 2 hours of fun while you follow the main story until lvl 56. Then you realize that you are gonna have to put up with a lot of frustration just to climb a small step, and that effort is exponential in nature. Of course, forget about trying more characters, it is a waste of time if you want to ever leave the wall you hit after obtaining awakening.

Enhancing gear is the most agressive and anti consumer mechanic I have seen in a serious game. It literally costs hundred of hours to get decent gear and then you have to pass dozens of probability checks in order to turn it into a competitive tool. And each attempt costs several enchancing resources, maybe one type, or maybe other, (or all of them) depending if you you fail or succeed. None of these are cheap and you will spend hours in the game gathering them.

This logic applies to every aspect of the game. No exceptions.

Events tend to introduce some currency, that you can grind in order to use other currency or resource, that will increase the chance to do X in order to obtain Y, which you need to obtain Z. And it is more probable that the process end up failing than succeeding. (Unless you spend real money on commodities, which frankly, don't even really help that much unles you have an unlimited supply).

Everything is designed to make you grind as fast and hard as you can to obtain resources that will sink in a bottomless pit when you try to convert them into something relevant.

So, what can you do with that system in a game that has awesome combat and exploration?

Once you reach softcap gear (gear which you can obtain before the grinding starts getting unbearable) you can explore a large chunk of the map. No elite grinding spots though. You can barely be competent in most of the efficient ones bare two.

You can also forget about PvP. You can enter, but you could last about a couple of blows against most regulars.

You can do lifeskill, but ever since a year or so thay nerfed heavily the money you make by everything that doesnt require expensive grinding (barter is the really only profitable lifeskill and it requires a lot of farming to get even started).

Basically, BDO starts you in an adventure where you feel like you can be anything, and then asks you, in order to progress, to dedicate more hours that you would do to your job and family or friends (or sleeping).

The worst part is that the hours don't really amount. You can fail a simple RNG check and lose the farm of an entire month. Or not fail it and still lose half of that amount just in failsafes and chance improvers.

I literally started a small business last year with way less hours than I spent in BDO and I got way more out of it. (It was also less frustrating, despite the obviously rough beginning).

When it's easier to make a living in real life than in a simulator it makes you think.

I got this game to play with friends. I was thinking like most MMOs that we could party up pretty easily and work together and maybe even do stuff faster together. We just found that it doesnt really give you any reason to do that and trying to play this game coop was pretty awkward. Now if you dont care about coop in the way that I did than this review is not for you.

This is... a very interesting game.

The obvious: The game is stunning. It just is. It's pretty. The character customization is pretty as heck as well. You will never go to any city and NOT see a ton of pretty anime girls around. Graphically, this game wins in all regards.

The less obvious:
Grind-fest.
I've played this game for over 300 hours, and my main account (aka the ONLY account I play on, because the others were just to play with the character creator) is level 57. That's pretty decent, but there are many enemies that will absolutely crush you if you're not careful. Sure, some of it is due to the class you pick, but when I'm creaming dozens of enemies, it's a little bit jarring when one buff guy can suddenly run up behind me and obliterate me, beause he knocked me down and the recovery is too slow for me to get away.
But levels aside, most of the QUESTS itself are just. Grinding.
I couldn't count on both my hands the number of quests I've done that demanded me to slaughter over HUNDREDS of enemies.
In fact, I currently have THREE quests that want me to kill 500 of a different kind of enemy. So to complete the quests, I have to kill 1500 enemies. That's pretty much an entire day's work, assuming I don't have anything else to do and that I get lucky.
Plenty of quests demand for you to kill 200, 300, 400, 500 enemies, and they keep coming.
I can excuse many quests that demand for the deaths of bosses, because. Well. That's just gaming. But I shouldn't have to kill thousands of enemies just for my little Black Spirit friend to be happy with me.

And even if you do all that, unless you're using combat XP item boosters, you're not gonna level up all too quickly.

So yes, this game is very much. A lot of killing.

For myself, personally? It's mindless. Buy lots of health potions and go ham. You kill most things quickly later on, so just keep an eye out for big boys that can end your life quicker than you can say 'oh no', and you're golden.

But most people do NOT have the time for this.

And there's a lot of mechanics in this game. Crafting, gathering, cooking, etc. I haven't touched any of them, unless a quest demanded it. There's guild things and nodes, but I'm a solo player. I don't touch them. I can't do one quest because of this, but it's not a main quest.

If you're wanting a pretty game to have some mindless combat and either really cool or cute characters? Go for it, but be prepared for about 60 popups every time you log in, talking about stuff you don't care about.

I don't particularly 'recommend' it, but it's not bad.

But don't buy the expansions.

It's ten dollars, and that's all it'll ever be worth at this rate.

I have so many things to say about this game. Most of them are good. But for those of you who want to know whether or not I recommend this game for you, I do not. 

Let me start by saying that this game was an accident. I bought this game and tried to get it to run for two hours, but my computer couldn't run it and I wanted a refund. Steam didn't give me one because it had been running for two hours. I dealt with it. When I upgraded my computer I came to try again.

What that means, is that you need to understand that this game is high-end. The graphics, were so good they'd make you cry. They'd bring tears to your eyes with how beautiful the scenery is. I found myself staring off into the distance, zoning out at the top of a mountain, in sheer awe. All of that was BEFORE they upgraded the graphics to the "remastered" version. Now the graphics are even BETTER! From what I can tell it didn't increase the spec requirements in the least. This game needs monster specs in your PC or you won't be able to run it competitively.

Competitively. That's another key word here, and, the main reason why I don't recommend this game. You see, this game, is hard. It's so hard that it's difficult to put into words. I guess the first thing I can tell you is that if you haven't bought the game and you are reading this review right now, then you will never be competitive, because someone who bought the game a few hours ago will have an innate advantage over you from the second you decide to buy this game. Competitively, this game is all about playing catch-up. And there are thousands of people with 5 years head start.

The max level for a character in this game is 100. This has been confirmed by the devs. The reason that this needed to be confirmed by the devs is because in the 5 years since its initial release there has not been a single person to level past 66 in this game.

If what I just wrote hasn't completely blown your mind, then maybe I can get your attention by saying that level is the LEAST important advantage and the MOST important advantage at the same time. Black Desert Online has a very interesting system. The higher your level, the more your level matters. Inversely, the lower your level, the less your level matters.

This is confusing because Black Desert is different than most games you're familiar with. In Black Desert, gear has no level requirement. Which also means that level is only important if you're high enough.

You get a situation where, a level 10 fully kitted in the best gear in the game (which no one has managed to complete yet) becomes a LITERAL god. The power swing is utterly astronomical. A level 10 in the best gear will beat the ass of a level 50 in average gear, without question.

Gear is the end all be all. Gear is the equivalent of "having the bigger stick". This gear, is so hard to come by that you might as well go to Las Vegas. I mean that literally not figuratively. To get this gear you have to pray to the GOD of this game that is commonly referred to as RNGesus. Random Number Generator. We are talking about rolling the dice and placing your bets. Luck is the ONLY factor that matters, the only upside to this situation is that it's not efficient to pay to win your way through it. It's a hard stuck situation. It's theoretically possible to brute force it with money, but you'd have to be Mr. Beast. None of us is Mr. Beast.


I'm getting off-topic. The point that I'm trying to make here is that if you buy this game, know that there are people out there with 5 year advantages over you. This game is for the hardcore. If you read this and think to yourself "I'm really hardcore, that sounds like the game for me!" then I want to stop you right there. This game's hardcore is different from the hardcore you're familiar with. The hardcore that you're familiar with is the soft-core of this game. There's a less friendly name for people like us who thought we were hardcore, I forgot what it was because I stepped back from this game months ago, it was too much for me. I thought of myself as hardcore, I took this game in stride and dove right in. I played for three months straight and no lifed myself to end-game knowledge. I learned EVERYTHING and I came to realize that I knew nothing. It all came full circle, there are people in this game who have spent YEARS trying to get ONE piece of gear. Often times that ONE piece of gear that you have is worth more than EVERY OTHER PIECE OF GEAR YOU OWN. That's the upgrade rate in this game. You get a set of gear and the next tier up, a single item from that new tier will cost everything you'd get from selling your current set. It goes on and on.

It's....I don't know what it is.


For those of you who want to call me out for being "elitist". You are damn right I'm an elitist. If you aren't, then you have no business looking at this game. When I quit I was four fifths of the way done building my Epheria Frigate and I was the proud owner of Vell's Heart, of which, at the time, there were less than 13 in existence. I did all of this and learned the insides and outsides of the game in only three months! I have the right to be proud.

If you have money to blow, time to waste, as far as investments go, at least the scenery is beautiful.

I’m really not a huge fan of these reviews with below 50h game time. I personally don’t feel like you can fully judge a MMORPG in this time. 
       
[u][b]P2W yes/no?[/b][/u]                
So first of all, what surely most people who are interested in Black Desert Online are wondering about. Is it Pay to Win? 
The answer would be a yes and no. You can p2w the enchanting but there is not much of a reason for it in my opinion. Also, it’s incredibly expensive to do so. In my nearly 3 1/2yrs of playing BDO it never had an effect on me, so if you aren’t aiming to play in the top <5% of the player base, this shouldn’t affect you at all. 
      
[u][b]Gameplay[/b][/u]    
Black Desert Online has one, if not the best action combat system currently on the market. (That is subjective of course) So if you are a fan of this fighting style in MMORPG’s you definitely came to the right place. You can either drag the skills to your Hotbar, or activate them with Key combinations, so its quite dynamic. 
    
BDO’s gameplay is highly focused on grinding, so you definitely have to be a fan of that. They also worked on the quest system in the last year and improved it a lot, which makes it a viable progress path now days. 
     
[u][b]Classes[/b][/u]    
There are 19 classes, which are genderlocked. Some classes have a male/female version which plays a bit different, so you should be fine, even with the genderlock in place and not limited in what you want to play!   
You can also create a test character which allows you to try out your chosen class on a higher level first, so see if you enjoy it or not! 
   
Beside that Black Desert has probably the best character editor you can find at the moment. It feels as close to a tool the developers use themselves as you can get. You can easily spend hours with it. Or if you aren’t into that, you can just load a preset from the beauty gallery. A tool where players can upload their character creation for others to use.     
     
[u][b]The World[/b][/u]      
Black Desert Online's Gameworld is massive. From deep woods, Ruins, over savannas, Coastal Areas, Massive Mountainous Areas, a giant desert up to a huge Ocean filled with many many islands. And all reachable without any loading screens.   
Since there are close to no options to teleport in BDO you really get a feeling for the vastness of this world, which is definitely a big plus in my book. But I can see that some people also might not enjoy it, that they cant just teleport half across the world. 


[u][b]Technic[/b][/u]    
The game has a vast amount of options of graphic sound etc, so it should pretty much run well on most machines. And it looks absolutely beautiful on the higher settings. 
BDO also supports 4K and even 8K resolution. 

[u][b]So, what is there to do? / Endgame?[/b][/u]    
Beside the grinding, Black Desert offers a massive professions system, called Lifeskilling in the game. There is a total of 11 Lifeskills, which you can all do, there is no limitation. Added to the lifeskill system, the game as a Node System. In basic, there are nodes all over the world, which can produce different goods, and you can/need to hire workers to gather these materials. 
          
BDO also offers Guild vs Guild PvP. Node Wars (Guild vs Guild fighting about special nodes) And Large Scale PvP. Each area has a Castle for which ownership guilds can fight. 
           
There is a good amount of World Bosses that spawn at set times.  
           
What Black Desert doesn’t have are Dungeons or Raids. If you are looking for that, this is definitely not your game.       
                 
[u][b]New Player Experience / Getting into it: [/b][/u]  
It's very easy now days to get into the game. The main story line, gives you lots of good gear to progress though the game and sends you right across all corners of the game world. They really improved this aspect of the game massively over the past 1 ½ years. 
     
But Black Desert also has some very complex systems that may need a while to get behind, but these aren’t mandatory mostly. What I personally enjoy about these is, that they aren’t complicated for the sake of being complicated but all make sense the way they are. 
And there are enough wikipages and guides that will help you to understand it all, if you happen to become interested in this aspect of the game.   
    
[u][b]Gear / Gear Improvement:[/b][/u]    
Unlike most MMORPG’s BDO has a steady gear progression. So new expansions don’t add a large number of new Items which make the old ones useless. They add stronger Items from time to time, but these mostly just add a little bit of extra power, so you won’t replace your whole gear every couple of months, once you get your hands on the higher tier items.   
For gear Improvement the game has an enchanting system that is highly focused on rng, but can be influenced with various technics and items. 
This is definitely one of the most complex aspects of the game. 
And I wouldn’t recommend newer players to get right into it, since it can become really expensive.   
If you don’t to enchant your gear, just farming silver and buying it is also a viable option, since every item can be sold via in in game marketplace. 

[u][b]Personal thoughts:[/b][/u]  
Black Desert Online is definitely not your usual MMORPG in some aspect, and does some things different, like no dungeons or raids, and the gear progression system. 
It's definitely not a game for everyone and by far not perfect. But I enjoy my time here quite a lot, and I would definitely recommend to give it a go.   
And if only to play around with the amazing character editor and the fun action combat system.

[b]Before I proceed onto the review, I must first mention that I have [b]NOT[/b] spent any money on this game other than the initial purchase.[/b]
------------------------------------
[b][i]*Sigh*[/i][/b] ...Black Desert Online

In the beginning hours (approx. 200-300+ or so), it was a fun and enjoyable game; combat was fun to make use of and exciting to see these sick animations being dished out by your character, ripping enemies to shred. Grinding, leveling up and enhancing your gears were a thrill! There was that sense of satisfaction and feeling rewarded for almost every little thing that was done.
...... Until you hit that point where you encounter this... Frustrating wall.
Progressing any further than that will only make you slowly lose the enthusiasm you had for this game like you had when first started out. You lose more than you gain, the cons outweighs the pros by a LARGE margin in almost everything you do.
Want to make hundreds of millions or billions of silver? Good luck m8, it'll take you months to set up something possibly worthwhile in which you become able to garner a decent income. Personally I tried that approach and only have ended up losing constantly or not making enough to cover the amount invested.
Almost [b]EVERYTHING[/b] this game has to offer is RNG. Save for gear enhancement (will talk about that later), RNG is applied from horse/pet breeding to get higher tiers, rolling good enough workers for your worker empire (which will become crucial in earning silver), good item drop from mobs (understandable, still, the chances are stupidly low) to marketplace bidding. Hell, even conversations with NPCs in order to get amity are RNG to an extent (although this feature is almost completely pointless).

The game severely limits you in ways that can affect your progression. Because of that, the game encourages blowing your cash on the cash shop. BDO isn't P2W per se - more so Pay to Progress, kind of a thin line between it and P2W, albeit ultimately leading to the same result as P2W. Still, I wouldn't exactly classify it as P2W however.
In whatever way you feel restricted in your experience during gameplay, there will most certainly be a solution for it.. In the cash shop, such as, but not limited to:
Inventory weight limit increase, inventory space limit increase, outfits/costumes which grant buffs or unique features tailored to specific tasks (processing, fishing etc..). Even increasing the chances of getting the skill you want for your Tier X horse..! There is a cash shop item for that too.
Most important of all is the Value Pack (we'll call it VP). The VP grants temporary buffs such as extra inventory/storage expansion slot and weight limit increase. But most importantly if you want to make more profit the VP grants "30% bonus to the Marketplace sales collection amount". Only way to get some of those are through earning Loyalty, which you get 100 of everyday, and even then still limited compared to spending money.

Grinding became an absolute chore. I'm not talking about just leveling your character up.
There's grinding to get more CP (Contribution Points) through quests and other means (mostly AFK alchemy/cooking - very time consuming).
Energy, which requires knowledge, and that can be a grind in and of itself, but isn't too bad since you'll acquire knowledge naturally as you play.

Gear enhancement? Pray with all your being and more that X amount of failstacks will suffice and silvers invested will be worth it..... Only for it to go down the damn drain and end up with lower enhanced gear. Don't get me started on boss and yellow grade gear... Especially accessories. You better have the power of RNGesus on your side.

You will inevitably encounter a point where you will have to AFK lifeskill for over 70% of your total hours (in my case approx. 900 of my hours or more was such). It is inevitable because it's necessary for making silver. And to make the best out of it, you'll have to buy value pack and costumes from the cash shop (as mentioned earlier). It is an extremely lengthy and time consuming task for it to even feel rewarding. And because of all the 24/7 AFK hours, your pc can become negatively affected.

As for the "multiplayer" aspect of this game: Well, this game doesn't really encourage you to interact with other players as really, most of the time spent will be alone. Only interaction you'll get is getting ganked by other players with better gear in grinding spots. There are the occasional understanding players who will tactfully ignore/avoid you even though they can probably crush you however.

Maintenance is a bitch because developers sometimes never deliver on what they promise. A supposedly 5hr downtime for maintenance ended up being 8-10hrs, only to screw up/corrupt games files. Compensation was granted, however IMO the given compensation was worthless.
Devs also manage to find ways to make gameplay less enjoyable with each update, like ruining balance to certain classes, adding things into the game no-one ever asked for. I mean NPC dating? Seriously?
Sure some events here and there was nice and fulfilling but that's it. They can only keep you in the game for so long.

I know that all I did was talk about the negatives, but truthfully speaking, most of the positives turns into negatives slowly over time, at least in my experience. Hence why I have uninstalled the game only not too long ago. If I have to list any pros:
- Beautiful graphics and decently optimized: I can get almost constant 60fps on the highest settings (1080p, GTX970) - bar for areas too crowded with players 
-  The overworld is nicely designed, large and open (probably too large for taste in fact), only downside to that is it comprises mostly of barren wasteland, ie; empty and mobs only appear here and there in their designated zones
- Combat is amazing! Although very simple yet fluid, it looks gorgeous and feels satisfying watching the epicness of your character slaying foes
- Great character creation

You'll be stuck in an endless loop where there is a sliver of hope of getting better gear: Grinding > get monies > watch as what little of your hopes left decide to leave you for some other lucky guy as you fail every enhancement > rinse and repeat.
So please do yourself a favour and save yourself from going down this never-ending rabbit hole. Do not buy this game. I wholeheartedly recommend against it.

[h1] THE GAME IS GOOD, BUT... [/h1]

[b] Rule Number 1 [/b] You will never be the best. There will always be someone better geared, better skilled. Don't worry about being the best, just do what you feel like doing. Always keep this in mind.

This game is NOT beginner friendly, but is getting better about it. If you know someone who plays, ask them for help.

[b] What do you do? [/b]
This game has many things for you to do and all of them are going to be tedious, long, and time consuming. Your goal is to find the thing you like to do and make it less time consuming, more efficient, and more fun. Some players call this game pay to win, but I would say it is Pay to Convenience. You can purchase things that help speed the game up if you rather not work towards speeding it up with in-game methods, 
but this is your game-play loop. Do a thing, get better stuff for that thing, do that thing a little better/faster.

As for actual things to do they can be broken into two main categories. Combat and Life Skill.

[b] COMBAT [/b] involves fighting. Fighting thousands of monsters, fighting bosses, fighting other players. The effects and the feel of the combat in this game are wonderful with many classes to pick from. You'll need combat gear to be good at killing things. Unlike most Life Skills, combat cannot be AFK'd, though training your character can be AFK'd slowly.

[b] LIFE SKILLS [/b] Gathering, Fishing, Hunting, Cooking, Alchemy, Processing, Horse Training, Goods Trading, Farming, Sailing, and Bartering. It's hard to summarize all these quickly, but some of these are complex, the rest are meant to be done AFK and you need Life Skill gear to do these faster/get more from them. All of these can be fun in their own way, though Hunting seems to have the least love in the game.

[b] OTHER THINGS. [/b] This game has a massive map to explore with tons of detail in it. I think about making a new account sometimes just so I can explore the map again. The cool thing about this, there is LIMITED FAST TRAVEL. You can auto-path your characters so you don't have to manually walk them and having many characters allows you to station them all over the map. This aspect of the game is my favorite and it gives a good reason to having many characters, though is not required.
While the Co-Op is a bit lacking, there are some nice social aspects to this game. You can customize your own house, see other player's houses. You can walk backwards into objects and you're character will lean/sit on them and pushing Q will change your pose which is all a nice Roll play element if you're looking for that. The character creator is still very good and with some skill, you can purchase outfits for your characters off of the central market from other players rather than spending real money. (Check the pearl Items Tab in the market frequently and check the pearl shop for items that are on sale. Those are likely to be on the market.)

This game is called an MMO, but is pretty heavily solo, especially if you are new and especially if you don't PVP. Very little for Co-Op, excluding being there at the same time for solo stuff. Though there are things like Guilds you can join and Co-Op monster zones.

[b] LASTLY [/b] This is a sandbox game. You make your own fun. This game is not a marathon and it is not a sprint. It is a journey around the globe. Things are meant to take time, a LONG time and they will take time. Many players have 10,000 hours in this game over years and years.  Most of my hours comes from doing things AFK in this game and I would still consider myself "New". So have fun, take in the sights along the way and do the things you feel like doing when you feel like doing them.

If you're considering playing this game, you need to understand that the minimum time spent to get your bearings is probably around 80-100 hours.
If you're writing a review and you haven't logged the time, it's not really helpful. However, it is absolutely true that if you don't like complex (and convoluted) games, this game is not for you, period. This game is extremely peculiar, in so many ways. You either enjoy that kind of stuff, or you don't.  

I played a lot some years ago, I lost the account, I rejoined the game a couple months ago, started from scratch. And my brain melted and seized repeatedly, even though I was already familiar with most of the game mechanics from before. Thankfully I joined the right guild, they saved me so much time trying to figure things out or having to look things up.

This is NOT a game for everyone. 

This game is NOT easy, unless all you want to do is relax, pick some flowers, catch some horses, decorate your house, or do fishing or alike. And I know quite a few players like that. They just enjoy the game for the scenery, doing quests, or doing ONLY fishing. It has a very steep learning curve, from the UI through understanding how things work, through constantly doing maths (especially if you choose to do lifeskilling). 

You don't have to engage in PVP. The game has a very rich PVE, and you don't have to do the endless grind to enjoy most of the content. And there is a LOT of content. If you do want to PVP, expect so much grind it will make santa cry. That said, the combat in the game is nothing like you've experienced before, in a good way. It's really, really good and complex.

The graphics, environment, even ambient sounds or sunsets - really amazing. Sunset in the desert, beautiful. City goes quiet, crickets come on, sun goes down, it's really enjoyable, and the different zones offer completely different ecosystems. Character creation, great. Customization, pretty great. Being able to just explore and even get lost (on the open ocean or the desert), great. Unless you're a hardcore player, there is always something to do in the game that's new and interesting. And they also add a lot of content and seasonal events, continuously.

Is it F2P?
Kinda. You can get away with it, but you don't really want to. It is NOT a P2W game. It is however pay for convenience and pay for looking at really pretty things all the time. In-game armor, even some end-game stuff, is terrifying. You will want to spend money on an outfit. However, they're giving away so much stuff these days that you don't need to spend money on that. Not really. The monthly "subscription" is about $15, and you can easily get it on sale for half off or more - worth every penny. I have spent about $80 total and got pretty much everything that's essential to your sanity (including 3 month subscription), and I still have $20 credit left. It would be super-easy to blow a lot of money in the game, they make a lot of cute/adorable pets, outfits, beautiful boat skins and carriages, horse equipment, etc. However, it is not necessary, and you can get a lot of that stuff on the marketplace for in-game money. Anyway, I feel like the $60 I've spent is accurate for the value of purchasing this game.

The bad:
* UI is super clunky and weird, takes time to get used to. It's really weird. Once you figure it out, easy peasy, but it's a steep learning curve.
* Some RNG stuff is really, truly bad & annoying. Not a deal breaker, and they're addressing a lot of that stuff right now. 
* Random weird shit will happen to you, like getting stuck in an alchemy tool, or your horse trips on a boulder and dies. or randomly walks off the cliff on it's own for no reason. It's part of the game, we just LOL at that stuff, like people having fishing chairs on their heads. Yes, after all those years, it's still buggy. To me, it's part of it's charm at this point. Nothing serious has affected me bug-wise, except mixing the main questlines (between LOML and mainland)
* Not doing the quests in order (if you're a new player) is suicide. DO NOT START A NEW CHARACTER ANYWHERE BUT VELIA! It is also imperative to do the MAIN QUESTS first and foremost, and then get distracted with everything else. Main quests are what unlocks a lot of the stuff in the game. I absolutely hate that part (the convoluted code spaghetti that is BDO - they really need to revamp the entire quest system), as I returned and made new char in LOML, which ended up being a massive time sink in trying to figure out what and why things aren't working as they should (progression for example). If you start in Velia, the on-boarding is amazing (quests and progression, introduction to lifeskilling, etc). If you start anywhere else, good luck, you will ragequit. They should not be allowing new players to start in the other two zones, period.
* There is a LOT of crap in the game. Like, stuff. Loot, items, lifeskill stuff, upgrade stuff, quest stuff, all that stuff multiplies like crazy and you won't know what is what for a long while. Stuff it in the warehouse, worry about it later. I feel like the amount of stuff in the game is way too much, and they either should shrink it (as if) or re-vamp the inventory system to provide some automation. There is also a lot of reading involved when it comes to items, each one comes with it's own essay and it's not always helpful. It's definitely a downer for me, although once you get used to everything in-game, you get a hold of it over time. Just don't try to figure everything at once. You'll blue screen. 

The good:
If you get over the initial hump, and you don't mind being patient with a convoluted system that takes a while to understand, the game can be very rewarding. I've played most of the MMOs at some point, starting with EQ beta. This one is by far the most engrossing fun MMOs on the market IF you like complex games. Unfortunately the steep learning curve kicks people out way before they had a chance to actually play it. I was a returning player and it took me a month to get to a point where I felt I have a hang on things again. It's a marathon, not a sprint. It's a game where it is understood that some things will take you months, chipping away one thing at a time. There is also a lot of AFK or semi-afk activities you can do that generate income, which is great for people who are busy and don't have time to grind all the time (like myself). You can also level up through those activities. You can setup workers on farms pretty early on, which cost close to nothing (you do need to feed them, but if you setup a worker on grain node, you can make beer immediately and thus feed the said workers - so costs you close to nothing to get your little empire going), you can do things like pound the corn batches (that your workers gather for you) semi-afk and sell the corn flour on the MP. This part is really helpful for people like me who do NOT have the time to grind constantly for money. I leave the character fishing overnight, and I'll do other lifeskills semi-afk as I work on other things (you know, RL). 

I do have to say that the game IS very Asian - and I mean it in the nicest way possible. I even have the Korean voiceovers turned on, it's so much better than the English version. There are a lot of very Asian cultural quirks in the game, even though they try VERY hard to be a "western" game - and they do succeed most of the time. Which is fine by me, but it might be a turn-off for some people who don't necessarily understand that culture. BDO is really very much it's own thing. You'll either love it or ragequit, there is no ambivalence possible, lol.

My Review:

I rate games based on how much value I get from them, based on a ratio of cost to enjoyment. This game has a retail price of $12.99 CAD, and I have put in over 1700 hours. In contrast, I have spent $100+ on AAA games that have given me less than 40 hours of enjoyment, and then had the audacity to charge me for DLCs. By my metric of value, Black Desert always delivers. 

So how do they make money off a $13 game? This is where a lot of people will complain: "Pay-to-win"
I have no problem with pay-to-win. It puts money in the developers' pockets, so they can continue to work on the game. It doesn't affect my personal journey with the game if others want to spend their money. In fact, it actually means that I don't have to. By having a cash shop, I don't need to pay for a membership every month. For just $13 down payment, I can play the game how often I want, and I never have to worry about my account getting held hostage until I make another payment.

Most other MMOs require you to pay anywhere from $12-$18 every month. If you decide to suspend your subscription, you can no longer play your game. This business model is archaic in my opinion. It feels like if I don't play, I'm losing money. If I had to pay $12 per month for BDO, I would have spent $576 on the game so far based on today's date. 

On the topic of Pay-to-Win, Black Desert is more like "Pay-to-Convenience". You don't actually need the items. You would need to pay an astronomical amount of money to actually gain any advantage. The only item that I would actually consider a "necessity" is the campsite, which allows you to fix your gear and buy potions/buffs without needing to go back to town, saving you minutes. At around $50 (one time purchase) for the campsite, the game is still under the price of most games. I got my tent at 50% off when there was a sale, so I paid even less.

Overall, I have probably put around $350 into the game. I bought the campsite, an item that allows you to summon your horse from anywhere, and numerous cosmetic outfits for my characters. I paid because I wanted to, because the game provides me enjoyment, and I want to support it. It didn't require me to subscribe, and hold a knife against my throat if I refused to pay for a month when I need to take a break. 

I enjoy grind-heavy games. I enjoy business models that reward the time you spend in game, instead of punishing you for not playing.

I start my session in the coastal town of [b]Velia[/b]. Player's Sailboats, Frigates and even tiny fishing craft are arriving and leaving the port behind the Storage Manager where I collect a few items for my morning outing. The crumbling ruins of the ancient bastion of [b]Cron Castle[/b] loom over the bay high on the cliffs, my destination is the forest behind it. Dodging the bandit guards who have infested this once noble fortress, I swop out my high level armour for a comfy Hunter's outfit forged from bones of a great beast and padded with skins of others. 

Checking my Matchlocks are in full repair, I reload and crawl forward on an unsuspecting [i]Wild Hog[/i], soon the meat I butcher and the skins I gather from [i]Deer[/i] frolicking behind him, will become crafted foods and clothing I will sell for profit on the [b]Player Market[/b]. I might even gain another [b]Life Skill[/b] level, thereby ensuring my top 5 Rank Badge I proudly float over my head is retained!
[list]
[*] [b]Hunting[/b] is one of the many [i]Life Skills[/i] you can focus on. Levelling up any [i]Life Skill[/i] allows for greater yields and procs better items.
[/list]
Time to check on my Worker Empire, these zealots are fuelled by Beer, or other items in truth but its way more fun imagining a sozzled workforce, so Beer they get. These wobbly goblins, giants and human indentured servants of mine are harvesting materials from nodes around the major cities, or pottering around in Workshops I own in [b]Port Epheria[/b] or the capital of [b]Calpheon City[/b]. They can pump out gear, upgrades for my [i]Trade Wagon, Horses or Boats[/i], clothing or cool furniture items for one of my 3 [u]player homes[/u].

My Guild members are bleating about wanting a large Guild Quest, I activate a kill order for them and the happy lot swarm off to a desert location. 2 of the new chaps get instantly lost as they enter the [b]Great Black Desert[/b], a place where your mini map and compass are non-functional, and reading the land is essential to finding your way. Many break down and construct a special [i]Compass[/i] for this task, but those in the know are never lost. Except sometimes. This same dynamic is present in the [b]Margoria[/b], the open ocean beyond the last scattered islands peppered with hidden Traders and sneaky Pirates.
[list]
[*][b]Guilds[/b] are primarily used to organise the in game mass PvP events, but many, like mine, are social / PvE focused.
[/list]
On a whim, I climb the mountain bordering the tiny winding mountain pass blocking coastal [b]Velia[/b] from the bustling city of [b]Heidel[/b] overlooking the swamps and farmlands. It is not easy, but i find a route and am rewarded with a view all the way to the Trina Knights fortress, perched on a peak flanking the only way into [b]Calpheon's[/b] farmlands, these tireless men and woman are under a constant barrage of Harpies, their fury fuelled by their queen...[i]Karanda[/i]. This particular World Boss is just about to spawn on schedule, I'll swop to my Valkyrie - waiting for her time to shine! A large group of players are waiting to drop her and loot the corpse, many get struck a massive AOE attack while a few low level players hang back waiting for the others to whittle her defences down.
[list]
[*][b]World Bosses[/b] spawn on a fixed schedule, so you can plan your visits to them. They have pretty low drop rates for their primary loot, [i]Boss Gear (Armour/Weapons)[/i] but drop a ton of other stuff including a collectible that rewards you with a [i]Boss Item[/i] at 100 count.

On my way down the hill I spot a white horse! A potential Tier 5 level if I can catch her! Checking that I have some sugar cubes on me, I start swinging a rope and approach. Later, I'll stable this new mount and breed her with my level 30, hoping to upgrade to a tier 7! Riding to the nearest military outpost that has an empty stable for me, I remember I should check my farms for weeds and bugs, its nearly harvest time and I need the special fruits to go into my Alchemy potions I'll be making for a later kill grinding session in the [b]Forest's of Kamyslyve[/b].
[list]
[*] [b]Horse Training+Breeding & Farming[/b] are more [i]Life Skills[/i], and a viable source of money making, selling to [i]Imperial (in game) or Player Markets[/i].
[*] Heading out and actively killing monsters is called [b]Grinding[/b] and is the primary source of XP and money from loot drops. While player level is uncapped in [b][u]BDO[/u][/b], it has a massively hyperbolic XP requirement over 61.

I'm up for a long ride now across the entire map, my options are running which takes forever... but at least levels my Stamina (can always ALT-TAB and read some emails!), grabbing one of my many horses, or even go hop on the intercity [b]Air Balloon[/b]....but not right now. Now I pull out my Trade Wagon, load up on some essential goods and set a course. Off we go! Leaving the city a looming thundercloud busts open and drenches me totally, I see some guys who are attempting to dry harvested animal hides giving up and heading inside. The sun will be shining the other side of the [b]Drieghan[/b] pass though as I climb snow-capped peaks.
[list]
[*] Travel in [b][u]BDO[/u][/b] can be done actively controlling your character, or using an Auto-pathing feature that allows you to AFK moving to a player set location. Walking across the entire map will take you about 1 full real world hour. A fast horse can do it in 15mins.
[*] [b]Trade[/b] is yet another [i]Life Skill[/i] and can be very profitable once leveled up, or a small alternate income to be made if you AFK travel a lot.

Before I log off, I'd better have a look at spending my hard earned cash from today. This'll be a long review, but surprisingly not even that in depth because there's a lot going on in this game.  

Bdo is very much not a sprint, and absolutely a marathon. It's near impossible for someone to reach end game in a short amount of time, but there are plenty of things to do(lots of different life skilling mostly) to take up your time, and your progression never technically stops, which is good. The game does look amazing(although there are quite a bit of pop-ins), and even with newly released mmo's, I still think Bdo is the one with the best graphics with very flash and fluid combat.  

Now, having said that, Bdo(at least at the time I quit approximately 2 years ago) was a very grindy game in every respect. As someone who doesn't like to repeat the same content over and over again, this game quickly became a chore and I ended up life skilling more than killing mobs. Combat that initially seemed cool quickly became dull as you just repeated the same combos over and over again. The many characters may delay this boredom, but it is inevitable unless you like that sort of thing. Mobs pretty much exist to be killed. In higher tier areas, it can get challenging, but there isn't really a reason to be farming there if you can't even kill the mobs efficiently.

To bring 'new content' to the game, there were regular events. Unfortunately, events were mostly the same thing, just with minute differences. Do a few quests(fetch, kill, talk etc), kill mobs for special drops or quotas, login daily; rinse and repeat. It gets quite monotonous, but this is a typical aspect of mmo's so it's not really something to complain about. There's only so much they can do I suppose. The problem is that everything plays the same(Anyone who's sunk more than a few hours will understand). 

The story...exists. If your comprehension skills are over 9000 and you like convoluted messes. 

The end game doesn't exist. No raids or dungeons, so no pve end game unless you count grinding. World bosses are there, but you can start them immediately and get some free loot(I'm not even kidding).

Pvp...exists, but personally I don't think it's very fun(I have fought quite a few people but it's rly disjointed). 

Personally, sieges(Mass pvp) feel boring. It's just a mess that'll blind you in seconds and takes a long while to set up. 

The rng systems implemented are a pain in the ass(to put it lightly), as progression isn't guaranteed, and you may blow billions of silver(Which could take months to acquire) in minutes trying to upgrade ONE piece of gear! I won't even bother mentioning the failstacks you need to prepare as well(which is probably one of the worst parts of this game). This rng system also applies to other things like uptiering horses(which isn't that relevant but they look good and obviously go faster the higher tier you go). 

The cash shop is also something of concern(Which apparently got much worse after I quit). The value-pack and other time-limited boosts like the blessing of Kama feels like a must have if you're going long term. The value pack costed about $20 or so AUD at the time I played, and it gave you more inventory, storage, xp gain etc, which is a damn big difference once you experience it. Fortunately, I don't really have a problem with anything else in there, and these boosts are the only things that felt truly pay-to-win. The costumes were pretty close though. You can also buy outfits to sell in the marketplace for ingame silver, but it's not worth unless you got a lot of $$$ to spend. 

Luckily, both the rng system and cash shop can technically be avoided if you use the marketplace, but you'll need to have quite a bit of patience and a lot of silver. So yeah....whales will definitely have the advantage. I'm not saying it's impossible to have fun and develop to endgame if you're f2p, but it's a damn chore that could take more than a year. If you're aiming to have all the best gear for just one character and you're f2p, then good luck. I'll check back in 10 years. 

Overall, this was a pretty good game but severely limited by terrible systems that any normal person would be annoyed by. The gear upgrade system is quite literally gambling, there is no other way to describe it. The only things that really keep people coming back is the beautiful graphics, combat and something I can only describe as a cross between sunk cost fallacy and stockholm syndrome. I.e. You spent too long with this game, invested too much, became attached(although you don't really know why) and now you're being held hostage and can't leave. It'll take quite a bit of willpower to drop it if you make it past a certain point, unless you got as mad as I did with the shitty systems and found better games to enjoy.

Did I mention that you'll also probably be running this game all day long? Yeah...the electricity bills aren't good...

If you read this far, you must really care about my opinion, or just don't have anything better to do. Either way, I'll end this with a simple question and answer. Do I recommend this game? 

Yea...nah, not really. If you got time to waste, go for it. If you like grinding, play this. If you hate rng progression, steer clear. If you're already in way too deep like I was, I commend you but also pity you. If you have more hours than I have(which there are likely many people), please tell me why.

I did enjoy my time with BDO, however there are a few issues I have with the game that ultimately led me to move on to greener pastures.  

BDO has a  beautiful, expansive world, interesting enemy design and excellent combat make for an exellent experience .  There's an incredible amount the player can do.  Crafting, cooking, horse taming and breeding, gathering, fishing, fighting, world bosses, PvP and repeatable quests are all available. It's a sandbox MMO so there's plenty to do if you feel like doing it.

  There's little reason to get invested in the game's story, however. It seems tacked on as an afterthought to lead new players from area to area.

Endgame is also very lackluster if you don't want to PvP.  It's all fine and good whilst you're levelling up, seeing new areas, killing new mobs, but when you hit the soft level cap and you've been there, seen and done that, it leaves you with little to do save for dailies and a very slow, repetitive grind.  There are engame PvE dungeons, but they are so far out of the way and require such high levels and top tier gear that they may as well not exsist for the majority of players.

  Despite the fact there is so much to do, the game does an atrociously poor job of explaining anything to the player, it's irritating to need an entire wiki and multiple youtube videos just to grasp the basics of how to play the game and how to progress.  Many essential mechanics are never even hinted at to the player or are so easily missed or dismissed as irrelevant that the player can end up gimping themselves for weeks of real time play as a result

BDO also is also like that psychotic girlfriend you used to date.  It'll demand your full, undevided 24/7 attention, even more than other MMO's and woe betide you if you aren't slaving away to please!  Even casual players leave the game on overnight or when they're at work to regain energy or to earn passive coin via fishing.  Not doing so is far more detrimental to your overall experience than you'd  think.

The game is so grind heavy you need evey single coin, every energy point, every bit of exp and consistant advancement just to have a chance at competeing and even then you can spend literal billions of silver, a months worth of grinding and selling items on the chance to upgrade a piece of gear only to have RNG dictate it blows up in your face leaving you with nothing but an empty gear slot and another months worth of grind just to get back where you were!

However the real killer for me was the community and the PvP mindset.  Simply put, BDO has the most toxic community I've ever experienced in an online game, worse than any other MMO, worse even than League of Legends at it's lowest and that's saying something.

The in game chat and naming policies are almost wholly unmonitored and unregulated.  Racism, homophobia and downright offensively degenerate garbage are mixed in with tasteless non-memes and mindless, repetitive spam. Actual questions about gameplay and mechanics are often ridiculed or ignored entirely.  The game cultivates and even encourages a bully boy mindset with unrestricted open world PvP that leaves everyone but the best geared players squabbling over scraps.

Anyone with more levels and better gear than you can and will butcher your character for whatever reason they deem relevant and you will have no way to fight back.  You simply cannot farm mobs in many end game areas of the world unless you get very lucky.  Geared players will often kill you  simply for passing through these areas in case you might decide to attack and kill 'their' mobs and take 'their' loot and exp.  Even farming resources , like cutting trees or mining rocks in the same area as another player is likely to see you casually murdered if they think they can beat you.  Don't even go afk to the bathroom whilst standing in a non-safe area unless you want a 50/50 chance of coming back to a dead character.

To compete at this level , as I said, you MUST dedicate your life to the game.  High level players have such a massively insurmountable head start over new players than unless you do no-life the game intensively for months or get incredibly lucky with drops, you will NEVER be able to compete. Or pay real money to catch up fast.

One of it's most debated points is the the fact that BDO IS Pay to Win.

I'll re-iterate that point. The game is Pay to Win.  This is NOT opinion.  It is FACT.   Many naysayers of the P2W arguement would claim the game is only pay for convenience.  Pets to pick up loot, costumes to give more exp, weight increases to carry more items and so on.  Some of these things can be obtained via the in game currency market, others cannot and in a game where every single coin and exp point is valuable, a player who spends real money for conveniences so they  can spend less time farming to earn that level or upgrade will have a massive advantage over a player who won't.

 More than that, costumes and pets can be sold for silver and then used to buy top tier gear from the marketplace, gear that a non paying player may have to grind for months to obtain and still never be able to afford. Even if this silver is used to buy upgrade tems, replacement items if upgrades fail and so on, it can shave off weeks and weeks of farm time. There are also some items and services that are impossible to obtain unless real money is spent.

 Even the most adamant defenders use the arguement that 'It would cost thousands to fully upgrade you with the best gear' so it's not pay to win.  However by that admission alone they acknowledge you CAN buy the best possible gear with real money if you're willing to pay for it. 

This game is all about the competitive PvP scene and you CAN use real money to gain an immediate advantage over someone who will not spend money.

I myself may play from time to time in the future with friends or just to revisit old areas and level up a new character, but I will never set BDO as my main, go to MMO because of this reason and the atrocious community.

So with all that in mind, if you want to experience it, wait for a sale, spend nothing in the store, get to soft level cap (56) whilst experiencing everything that makes BDO fun ,then move on unless you decide that the rancid community, putrid attitudes and extremely lengthy months long grind that can be removed by spending real money don't bother you.

BDO has great graphics, and smooth combat animations, the appearance of multifaceted sandbox mmo, but at its core its very hollow. So if you are looking for a very pretty game with little substance inside then BDO is for you, if you looking for something with something deeper then look else where.

This game has a very badly written main story, ofc people would say no one plays a mmo for its story, but fundamentally mmo is still a form of RPG, and as such cannot escape the need of a story. Not only is the plot poorly written and cheesy, sometime even the dialogues are poorly written and hold little logical sense.

The combat initially is exciting, feels great with smooth and flashy animations, but it get repetitive fast, once you pass the initial excitement period, all that's left is endless grinds over the same areas on the same mobs for the same loots. While other games might at least cover it up with some sugar coating, this game leaves its grind out in the open with no sugar coating, even many of the story quests are as simple as kill X monsters, then the next quest is kill X more of the same monsters, instead of trying to do something interesting with each mission.

Not only do you have to deal with boredom while grinding, you also have to deal with other players trying to take your grind spot, which is perhaps the best part of BDO, its PVP. If you into pvp then maybe this game is for you, but do keep in mind its not without issues, for example if someone out gear you, instead of pvp becoming competitive, it just becomes a bullying fest. If you internet connection is slow, you might get lags and die before you get to see whats going on. Lastly, the system isn't balanced in the sense that whoever get CCed first will die, so a fight seldom last more than a few seconds, and if both side are similarly geared, the fight is largely luck determined by who landed a CC first.

Then comes its world famous life skill, again at a glance it looks great, a lot of different life skills you can specialise in and make silver, but at its core its still hollow and grindy. at least half of its life skills are AFK based, meaning you set up whatever your character want to do and you can go do something else, the few that isn't AFK, you basically repeat the same grindy nature like combat, for example with gathering, you just keep killing a bunch of animals and gather meat from their carcass.

With that said, considering the amount of times I've been playing this game, the amount of money I spent in it is still kinda worth it, as it costed less than buying a new game very month, but whether its better to keep buying new games or spend similar amount of money into one P2W game is entirely up to you.

This game has a ton of potential but unfortunately, there are some MAJOR issues holding it back. let's start with the positives:
1. Gorgeous graphics from the player models to the environments. Top notch for an MMO.
2. Deep economic system
3. Great crafting
4. Fantastic combat system
Now for the negatives, and unfortunately there are many:
1. Inventory management. this is the number one offender IMO. They say this game doesn't require a subscription but that's not entirely true. You start out with a 30 day value pack that grants you 16 extra slots of inventory, extra carry weight and bank slots. Obviously you are going to fill that up pretty quickly and then when the 30 day mark rolls around you are pretty much grid locked. Your only choice is to dispose of a ton of valuables or (you guessed it!) buy another 30 day value pack for 15 bucks. you really can't play the game with out it so go ahead and plan on spending 15 bucks a month for inventory.
2. Overpriced cash shop. As I stated above, you can pay 15 bucks for inventory or a whopping 30 bucks for a costume in the cash shop which is absolutley rediculous. They make a half hearted effort by allowing a lottery in game with a chance of winning these things with in game currency but who wants to hassle with spending hours of game time bidding on items in a loterry against hundreds of other players? i managed to snag 2 value packs for my efforts in the lottery and thats over 90 days of heavy playtime and countless attempts. 
3. Pretty much zero social activity. The world initially seems alive and vibrant with players running around everywhere, but you soon realize everone is pretty much doing their own thing. There is little to no reason to form a party because 90% of the game doesn't require a party. 
4. Unbalanced difficulty. You will sonn find out that the mobs are either way too easy or far too difficult. You will slice through them like butter in level appropriate zones or you will get one shotted in higher level zones. Furthermore, even if you can survive a few mobs in the higher level zones, there's really no xp or loot bonuses that offer any incentive for taking on these more difficult challenges. 
5. Loot drops and  in game gear is lack luster to say the least. Most of the gear outside of the cash shop leaves a lot to be desired in the visual sense. 
6. Steep learning curve. Plan on heading to youtube if you really want to learn the game because the in game tutorial sucks. The game is complex and that's not necessarily a bad thing but, I feel like the devs could have done a much better job with the tutorial. 
7. AFK leveling. Still scratching my head on this one. I'm not sure why the devs felt like this was a good idea. Most people make their in game currency by just leaving their computers on all night while their character fishes AFK. Dumb. 
8. Cash shop steering. As I stated before, they give you a 30 day value pack with the explorers addition. The value pack is designed to steer you into the cash shop. You simply can't play the game without it. Without it you not only lose inventory slots, carrying weight and bank slots. But you also take a 30% hit on the in game market. That's huge when it comes to in game currency. All this is designed so that you head back to the cash shop every month and plop down that 15 bucks for the value pack. Not to mention, there are items on the cash shop that give you advantages in crafting upgrades, convenience and even PVP.
9. Horrible, HORRIBLE gear upgrading system. it's expensive, it's redundant, it's chance based and it's way more annoying and frustrating than fun. that's all you need to know. if you decide to take a spin on this game, I HIGHLY recommend you just buy your gear from the auction if you can.

[*]It has a lovely story which you can follow (there are 10000s of quests) but it hasn't got an ending. The game regularly gets new content and it is constantly changing as it is being improved, developed.
[*]It has beautiful graphics and an amazing soundtrack. Wherever I go, I just want to stop and stay there for a while until I can completely listen to the songs. Sometimes I don't even want to actually play this game but only listen to the wonderful songs in it.
[*]The game (and its story) never ends and there isn't a well-defined goal. It gives you complete freedom, you have to find the activities which you like the most.
[*]The world of Black Desert is vast. I haven't even explored half of it. You will always find secrets (which can actually be a purpose of playing it).
[*]The community is extremely friendly. Throughout my gameplays, I have only received heartwarming words and helpful suggestions. Players often give up their own goals just to help.
[*]The game has a functional anti-cheat. I have never seen cheaters or even unfair players.
[*]I think the sentences [i]Enjoy your journey not just your goal[/i] and [i]Best Day Online[/i] describe this game fairly and accurately.
[/list]
I will also try to describe when Black Desert might not be an ideal game for you:
[list]
[*]It is quite time-consuming. If you often don't play it for long periods of time (e.g., months), you might find that the game has considerably changed or you have missed a lot of important opportunities. Activity is key in Black Desert.
[*]The game is complex and it takes time (this means years) to learn how to play it and to get gear. It supports slow and gradual progression. You won't get everything in the beginning.
[*]Don't expect a shooter game-like experience or overly modern elements. This game is set in a medieval fantasy world (which is one of the reasons why I love playing it). You use some kind of sword most of the time. In order to reach distant places, you usually travel on a horse. Getting the appropriate horse is also beautifully detailed process.
[*]It is grindy and certain outcomes depend on random factors. You have to accept the fact that sometimes you are lucky, sometimes you are unlucky.
[*]And finally, probably the most important: If you tend to compare yourself to others too much or you have a competitive mindset, this is most likely not your game. In Black Desert, you will always find people who are far ahead of you. You simply don't have a chance to reach them because they have spent several years on improving their character and skills. Fairly, you will also have to spend the same amount of time and make the same effort.
[/list]
Black Desert is an ideal game to be played solo, at your own pace, but it can also be played together with friends, which is also so wonderful. I also recommend that you join a guild which shares your interests. There are endless social activities to do and magical places to discover, or just try watching the beautiful stars at night while you're visiting an oasis in the desert. You can even learn to compose and play your own music.🌸

6k+ hours played over 3 years. Here's some info and tips:

* TLDR: I would recommend it to anyone who likes MMOs and I would recommend you play casually. It's an MMO. That means long term progression, grinding, massive exploration, guilds, PvE, PvP, character creation, outfits, and gear building (theorycraft). It's a marathon not a race, don't play it excessively. Progression is mostly rng and you can technically p2w. All the classes look awesome and play differently so you should be able to find something to suite yourself nicely.

* Play whatever class you want. Like any game in the history of games there will be a meta class that just destroys everything in PvP and a best grind class but just forget all that until you have explored and tried the game for a while. It has a little class for everyone -IGN probably. 

* Season servers. Play season servers to progress incredibly fast. Seasons last aprox 3 months with one starting Apr 6 2022 with the new region and class. Even veterans play seasons for the easy rewards. If you're going to try the game, play it for a full season first. Season servers can get crowded during prime time of the first couple weeks. 

* RNG. The progression system is rng enhancement and you often loose progress if you fail on your main equipment. Season enhancement is stupid easy. The npc Jetina has some non-rng progression you can do (which I did because my luck is the standard for trash). The game is a marathon not a race so if you expect to 1 tap all your gear to the highest level, you're a donut, or rng carried. You can protect your enhancements using cron stones though so just do that if you like.

* P2W? Yes but not reasonably. You can pay irl money to get silver (in-game currency), so technically p2w. But this will cost you anywhere from $5k to $100k to start reaching endgame so just don't. Let all the middle eastern princes sell the premium items on the market for you. You can easily play efficiently without paying irl money for some of the speedy conveniences offered in the pearl shop (the cash shop). They have gotten way better about this recently as well. There is also a loyalties shop where you can get some premium stuff from just logging in. Look up a free to play guide to decide for yourself if it's too p2w. 

* Pick whatever style you want. There are a few main styles/activities to play/do.
     ~ Lifeskilling: You can hunt and butcher animals, gather materials, fish, sail and barter at sea, cook, perform alchemy, etc. As of March 2022 hunting makes huge money and cooking/alchemy are pretty good.
     ~ Grinding: Yes, you will run in circles killing mobs. The action combat makes the grind fun sometimes. You will make the most money doing this at almost every progression point in the game. Grind on season servers if you're new. Don't push yourself and burn out grinding. Max out your season character over the 3 months (just a little each day and some extra on the weekends if you want) then look for npc Jetina and go from there. It's a marathon not a race, don't trying to be endgame in 4 months.
     ~ PvP: You can technically make money doing this but Pearl Abyss (game company) wants this to be more of a recreation than a progression thing. There is a season PvP server and season arena so you won't get slapped by endgame players if you want to try BDO's PvP at a competitive level. New gear capped arena coming soon too. 

* Dungeons. They have currently added two dungeons with plans for at least 2 more soon. The main grinding of the game is done in open world at monster zones but the dungeons make huge money with the weekly quests and are still repeatable for rewards afterwards. 

* Co-Op. The game is mostly a solo MMO with other people around in the world. There are a few party grind spots. If you join a guild you can get into skirmishes with your guildies against other guilds in the open world. Guilds can do Node Wars Sun-Fri and higher end guilds do Sieges on Saturdays as well. Node Wars are guild vs guild fights to take control of a node and sieges allow you to bring your entire 100+ man guild to fight others over an entire region of the map. Sieges can make some pretty good money too. 

** Again, the game is a marathon not a race. I like BDO because the combat is great and I like MMOs in general. It has a some p2w and meta classes like most games. The only draw back is the rng system. If you're willing to accept a little rng and some extra grinding when you inevitably fail something then the game is great. Don't play it excessively, just casually make some gains, try a new class every season, do some quests, explore, join a guild, lifeskill, and do whatever. If you get lost just follow the main questline and remember to play on a season character.

[b] Pros: [/b]
[list]
[*]I barely see people acknowledging that almost everything from the pearl shop, like costumes, can be bought for free through the marketplace with ingame currency (silver). IMO, BDO is NOT pay to win in a sense that you really don't have to pay anything to obtain almost everything in the game. It is just extremely hard to for a few things like PEN blackstar but it's possible and that's all that matters to me
Paying to progress is a legit option though, but if someone has a lot of cash to burn, I like BDO for giving them the freedom to spend it on it. It is how free to play players are able to get pearl shop items. Players who buy pearl shop items can sell them for silver and buy their way to endgame gear through the marketplace. Players with money are also funding the game allowing free huge updates like the recent expansion of the world adding O'Dyllita. It helps everyone
Just play A LOT to progress if spending money is not an option. That is what I mainly do, and I'm doing fine obtaining endgame gear.
Sometimes events give free pets, inventory expansions, costumes/underwear, maids/butlers, furniture sets, etc
[*]THE best character creation right now in any MMO. Different parts of the face, the whole body including weight and size of body parts, a lot of hair to choose from, etc., can be edited through sliders.
[*]Classes are well-defined/detailed with unique animations, costumes, and hairstyles
[*]The graphics are insane and SO beautiful. For me, I love traveling around the world and immersing myself in the different places one can go to like Florin which is this small herbal town that looks magical with remastered mode on. The best graphics in any MMO right now hands down
[*]The best combat system which is action combat. Grinding is tolerable for me because the combat is so fun. Players can make different builds through the skill menu
[*]For someone who doesn't like boss raids or dungeons, BDO is great because this game is almost 100% solo, meaning almost everything can be done alone. Though in world boss fights a lot of players are needed but a person can go and fight them alongside others on their own terms
Being in a guild can be very helpful. Guilds can focus on different aspects of the game like sea monster hunting or PVP, so someone who enjoys PVP can join a PVP-focused guild
[*]This game is truly sandbox meaning there is a lot of freedom to do whatever is in mind right at the beginning. There are no restrictions to, for example, start fishing or horse training
The best thing about this is that I can go anywhere I want to. It is a huge open-world game.
Not completing the main questline barely restricts anything. I still have a lot to finish on my main character and almost everything is unlocked for me already. Though, for some NPCs, like merchants, won't give their services if the player doesn't have the required knowledge, which are sometimes obtained by doing the main questline
[*] There are a lot of ways a player can make silver. Lifeskilling is a legit way and can bring tons of them. Grinding is another option. I personally don't do both as often because it is not for me, but I still manage to make a decent amount as I play by other ways like killing weekly rift bosses or participating in events
PVE content is definitely there. I personally enjoy sailing very much. There is actually a pirate system so I like to be a pirate and discover islands out in the ocean
[/list]
[b] Cons: [/b]
[list]
[*]I absolutely hate the enchanting system. I'm currently enchanting endgame gear and it makes me want to die at times. It is dependent on RNG so a 90% chance of success can still fail a bunch of times. Going through this system without spending a dime of real money is possible, but it takes an incredible amount of patience and commitment. Enchanting isn't necessary to progress since all gear can be bought from the marketplace, but it is usually the fastest way because it can take a lot of time to save up enough silver for that
[*]This game is NOT a sprint but a VERY long marathon. It can take a year or more to reach soft cap or endgame competitive for PVP, so patience and commitment are the keys to progressing IMO
[*]Classes are gender-locked. IMO, it's not a big deal because all of them are very unique and detailed. Some classes like striker and mystic, ninja and kunoichi, musa and maehwa, and wizard and witch are similar in their preawakening combat though, and are considered to be each other's gender counterparts
[*]Paying to progress being an option gives an advantage in PVP over free to play players. For many it makes BDO pay to win but as a PVE player who never PVPs, it doesn't affect me
[*]I'm personally not a huge fan of the grinding. I cannot do it for more than 3 hours because it gets very repetitive and boring. Some people don't mind it and can do it for way longer. Grinding is a huge aspect of the game but it can be somewhat avoided
[/list]

Anyway I really do recommend it if it seems like it's for you. It's 10 dollars. Maybe get it on sale. Like I said it is not for everyone but I'm someone who really enjoys my time in the game as a casual endgame PVE player. It doesn't deserve the bad rep it has IMO. It's a very good MMO overall.
